coverageAssessment.underrepresented: Pre-modern global science, biological origins, observation technologies, dated contributions by people, substantial named encounters.

coverageAssessment.selectionResult: Retain all 112 released event records. Promote 75 to the main path and keep 37 as supporting detail; add 64 dated contributions/cases for 139 main milestones. The target range guides depth; it is not enforced as a quota.
coverageAssessment.geography: African archaeological evidence; Greek, South Asian, Arabic, Persian and Chinese intellectual traditions; European and North American physical science; Soviet spaceflight; encounters in Australia, Zimbabwe, Belgium, Japan/Alaska and the United States added to retained Canadian, Brazilian, French, New Zealand and Iranian histories. This is uneven, selective coverage, not a global ranking or demographic quota.
coverageAssessment.contribution: People are credited for dated work and source-specific roles. Experimental collaborators, predecessors, assignees, witnesses, reviewers and advocates are distinct. All event people resolve to canonical names, aliases or explicitly erroneous legacy search labels.
coverageAssessment.narrative: One chronology interweaves observation, models, biology, instruments, destructive uses, reported encounters, investigations, spirituality and records access. Every main entry has an editorial-context or source-supported connection. No proximity or thematic parallel is entered as a factual influence edge.

candidates.title: Early Homo sapiens evidence at Jebel Irhoud
candidates.reason: This evidence gives the chronology a deep African starting point and makes human origins a changing research problem rather than a single birthplace or sudden event.
limitations: The dated material is associated heated flint; the estimate is not a direct calendar date for every fossil.
These finds do not identify the first Homo sapiens or establish one geographic origin for the species.

candidates.title: An ochre drawing at Blombos Cave
candidates.reason: The object makes early graphic practice visible through material evidence, while leaving a clear boundary between identifying deliberate marks and interpreting what those marks meant.
limitations: Context dating estimates the archaeological phase, not the exact moment of drawing.
The pattern does not establish language, a particular belief, or a decipherable symbolic message.

candidates.title: Aristotle argues for a single cosmos
candidates.reason: A chronology of knowledge includes durable frameworks that were later challenged; Aristotle's account makes the premises behind one influential picture of the heavens open to inspection.
limitations: The surviving argument is historical natural philosophy, not evidence that only one planetary system exists.
The approximate date cannot be resolved to a precise year or day from the inspected text.

candidates.title: Epicurus reasons about innumerable worlds
candidates.reason: The letter distinguishes the history of possible worlds from their detection, giving readers a clear example of a speculative argument that predates observational tests.
limitations: Ancient ‘worlds’ cannot be equated without qualification with modern exoplanets.
Neither a precise composition date nor evidence of extraterrestrial life follows from this passage.

candidates.title: Aryabhata explains apparent stellar motion
candidates.reason: This entry broadens the history of mathematical astronomy and shows why precise readings matter: a rotating Earth is a specific proposal, not automatically modern heliocentrism.
limitations: The following stanza has a conflicting-looking account; the inspected translation discusses this textual difficulty.
The text locates Earth centrally and must not be presented as the modern Sun-centred planetary system.

candidates.title: Ibn al-Haytham investigates light and vision
candidates.reason: The work connects theories of perception to inspectable procedures, adding an Arabic scientific tradition to the chronology without reducing a cumulative history to one inventor.
limitations: The entry does not claim that Ibn al-Haytham invented experimentation or the scientific method.
Only the specified direct-vision passages are assessed; this is not a validation of the whole historical optical system.

candidates.title: Shen Kuo records magnetic-needle behaviour
candidates.reason: A precise account of an ordinary instrument reveals how useful knowledge can advance through comparison and admitted uncertainty, without requiring a complete theory of magnetism.
limitations: This is not a claim that Shen Kuo invented the compass or discovered every aspect of magnetic declination.
The work's compilation date does not date each reported observation precisely.

candidates.title: Al-Tusi reworks mathematical astronomy
candidates.reason: The manuscript places mathematical model building in a wider scholarly geography and preserves a concrete contribution without assuming that every later resemblance proves direct borrowing.
limitations: The Arabic treatise was not fully translated or mathematically reconstructed in this review; the diagram's identification follows its custodial catalog.
The inspected sources do not establish a transmission path to Copernicus.

candidates.title: Gutenberg's workshop prints the Latin Bible
candidates.reason: The milestone concerns the reproducibility and circulation of texts, a practical condition for comparing claims and building shared knowledge across readers separated by distance.
limitations: This is a European Bible-production milestone, not the beginning of printing worldwide.
The exact distribution of work among all workshop staff and later artisans is not recoverable from this guide.

candidates.title: Copernicus publishes a Sun-centred planetary system
candidates.reason: The book changed the arrangement under discussion and made it available for calculation and criticism; publishing a model and establishing all its claims remained different tasks.
limitations: The book's historical planetary model should not be equated in every detail with current astronomy.
Osiander's anonymous prefatory account of hypotheses is distinct from Copernicus's own text.

candidates.title: Kepler publishes a revised orbit for Mars
candidates.reason: The episode connects better observations with willingness to revise a preferred geometry, while preserving the separate contributions of the observer and the mathematical investigator.
limitations: The third planetary law belongs to Kepler's later work, not this 1609 publication.
This review inspected a primary diagram and custodial account, not the complete Latin calculations or a numerical replication.

candidates.title: Galileo publishes telescopic observations
candidates.reason: The publication made new observations available for checking and debate, while showing that instruments extend perception through an interaction of manufacture, repeated use and interpretation.
limitations: These observations did not by themselves establish every part of a Sun-centred cosmology.
Galileo's later observations of Venus's phases are not imported into this publication.

candidates.title: Descartes publishes his Discourse on Method
candidates.reason: The entry makes methods themselves part of the history of inquiry: rules for judging claims can be proposed, scrutinised and revised alongside claims about nature.
limitations: This publication did not originate all systematic reasoning or experimental practice.
Descartes's wider metaphysical arguments are not treated as experimentally established findings.

candidates.title: Newton publishes the Principia
candidates.reason: The book made a broad range of motions answerable to shared mathematical arguments, illustrating the explanatory reach of a model without making its historical form final.
limitations: Later additions, including the General Scholium, must not be dated to the 1687 first edition.
A mathematical account of gravitational attraction is distinct from an explanation of its underlying physical mechanism.

candidates.title: Faraday demonstrates electromagnetic induction
candidates.reason: The experiment made a new relationship between electricity and magnetism measurable, with apparatus and repeatable changes connecting an observed effect to later mathematical accounts.
limitations: The date marks one documented experiment within a continuing programme of investigation.
The effect depends on changing conditions; the experiment does not describe a permanent current from an unchanging arrangement.

candidates.title: Darwin and Wallace's selection papers are presented
candidates.reason: The episode joins a powerful biological explanation to a visible record of overlapping discovery, reminding readers that scientific credit and communication are part of knowledge production.
limitations: These writings do not supply the later genetic account of inheritance.
Natural selection is not a ladder of inevitable progress or an explanation of the first origin of life.

candidates.title: Maxwell publishes an electromagnetic theory of light
candidates.reason: The paper linked apparently different phenomena through a quantitative theory, showing how agreement between independent measurements can strengthen an explanation while its conceptual machinery continues to change.
limitations: The paper's mechanical-medium assumptions belong to its historical formulation and should not be silently presented as current requirements.
The publication is a theoretical account, not the later experimental production and detection of radio waves.

candidates.title: Tesla patents a motor driven by alternating currents
candidates.reason: A dated patent makes Tesla’s engineering contribution inspectable through a specific mechanism, connecting electrical theory with practical machinery and transmission of mechanical power.
limitations: A patent documents this claimed invention; it does not establish that Tesla alone invented alternating current technology.
The patent contains no evidence of exotic energy sources or later claims about secret technologies.

candidates.title: The Curies and Bémont report evidence for radium
candidates.reason: The report joined chemical separation, electrical measurement and spectroscopy to identify a new radioactive element, showing how multiple kinds of evidence can reinforce a discovery.
limitations: The sample still contained much barium; this paper did not report isolated pure radium metal.
Radioactivity is a physical phenomenon; the authors’ historical energy speculation should not be repeated as a modern conclusion.

candidates.title: Planck introduces finite energy elements in a radiation calculation
candidates.reason: The calculation introduced the constant now called Planck’s constant into radiation theory, providing a foundational quantitative problem and tool for later quantum physics.
limitations: This was a radiation calculation, not the completed quantum mechanics of the 1920s.
The inspected translation identifies the 1900 proceedings; no exact presentation day is asserted from this copy alone.

candidates.title: The Wright brothers make four powered flights
candidates.reason: The flights made powered human flight a documented engineering achievement, combining propulsion and control while exposing the practical limits of the first machine.
limitations: These were short experimental flights with significant control difficulties, not a mature transport system.
The entry records the Wright achievement without treating all earlier aviation work as absent.

candidates.title: Einstein formulates special relativity
candidates.reason: The paper changed how space, time and motion could be related mathematically, creating a theoretical foundation whose consequences could be tested by observation.
limitations: This entry concerns special relativity, not every paper Einstein published in 1905.
A theoretical publication is not itself an experimental confirmation of all its consequences.

candidates.title: Rutherford explains scattering with a concentrated atomic center
candidates.reason: The paper shows how unexpected experimental results can force a structural model to change, making scattering a quantitative probe of the interior of matter.
limitations: Rutherford explicitly states that these deductions did not determine whether the central charge was positive or negative.
This 1911 model was not a complete modern account of nuclei or electron structure.

candidates.title: Leavitt relates variable-star periods to brightness
candidates.reason: The relation supplied a way to compare stellar brightness systematically and, after calibration, supported the astronomical distance measurements that expanded the measured scale of the cosmos.
limitations: The circular calls for determining an absolute distance scale; it did not already supply a calibrated cosmic distance ladder.
March 3 is the date printed at the circular’s close, not a claim about the first day of discovery.

candidates.title: Einstein submits the field equations of general relativity
candidates.reason: This mathematical formulation made gravitation part of spacetime geometry and supplied a framework for later cosmological models, while leaving predictions to independent observational testing.
limitations: November 25 is the submission milestone; it should not automatically be treated as the paper’s publication date.
The paper’s completion of a theory was not simultaneous confirmation of every later gravitational prediction.

candidates.title: Payne uses atomic physics to analyze stellar atmospheres
candidates.reason: The monograph helped turn spectral classification into a physical account of stellar temperatures and composition, while its qualifications reveal the difficulty of interpreting disruptive results.
limitations: The thesis’s qualified wording must not be rewritten as an unqualified announcement of today’s accepted stellar composition.
The publication year is established; the May 1 date in the preface is not treated as an exact publication day.

candidates.title: Hubble’s Cepheid results place spiral nebulae beyond the Milky Way
candidates.reason: The measurements established an observational route beyond the Milky Way, turning a long-standing debate about spiral nebulae into a question answerable with stellar distances.
limitations: The 1925 distance scale was preliminary and should not be presented as today’s accepted numerical distances.
This extragalactic-distance milestone is distinct from Hubble’s 1929 velocity–distance paper.

candidates.title: Lemaître links cosmic expansion to galaxy redshifts
candidates.reason: The paper connected mathematical cosmology with an observable velocity–distance relation, providing an expansion interpretation before Hubble’s better-known 1929 observational paper appeared in print.
limitations: Its distances and estimated expansion rate were preliminary; the 1927 model is not the complete modern cosmological model.
The inspected text is a 2013 translation of the 1927 original, not the modified 1931 translation.

candidates.title: Schrödinger submits a wave equation for atomic energy levels
candidates.reason: The paper gave atomic quantization a differential-equation formulation, creating a calculational method for energy levels and opening a major route into quantum physics.
limitations: This first paper does not represent every formulation or interpretation of quantum mechanics.
The mathematical treatment supplies no evidence for quantum explanations of consciousness or unidentified objects.

candidates.title: Hubble reports a galaxy velocity–distance relation
candidates.reason: The measured relation connected galaxy distances with spectral shifts and became a central observational constraint on cosmology, alongside earlier theoretical work on expansion.
limitations: The inferred distance scale and proportionality constant were preliminary; the paper warns that the range and sample were limited.
Hubble’s paper is not the first theoretical proposal of an expanding universe.

candidates.title: Jansky reports radio waves from beyond the Solar System
candidates.reason: The report extended astronomical observation into radio wavelengths, illustrating how an engineering problem can reveal a new source of information about the sky.
limitations: The Nature page exposed the opening passage and metadata, not the full letter; the historical development is corroborated by NRAO’s archive account.
The astronomical origin described here is not evidence of an intelligent transmission.

candidates.title: Watson-Watt and Wilkins demonstrate radio detection of an aircraft
candidates.reason: The trial made radio detection of aircraft a practical development path, linking instrument design, organized research and the later interpretation of airborne radar observations.
limitations: This was a British demonstration, not a claim that radar had a single inventor or no predecessors elsewhere.
The original report, apparatus data and trial log were not inspected; the source is NPL’s institutional history.

candidates.title: Turing formalizes computation and its limits
candidates.reason: The paper made computation a precise mathematical object and showed that some general decision tasks are impossible, foundations distinct from building a physical computer.
limitations: The machine is a mathematical construction; this paper did not announce a working electronic computer.
The journal volume is labeled 1937, while the paper’s two parts appeared in 1936; year precision avoids obscuring that distinction.

candidates.title: Meitner and Frisch explain uranium splitting
candidates.reason: The letter turned surprising chemical evidence into a nuclear mechanism, separating experimental identification of products from the physical explanation of the energy released.
limitations: The letter is an interpretation of experimental findings, not an account of a functioning reactor or weapon.
Chemical discovery, physical interpretation and subsequent experimental confirmation should not be collapsed into a lone-person breakthrough.

candidates.title: Shannon defines a mathematical theory of communication
candidates.reason: The theory supplied quantitative limits for transmitting information through noisy channels, giving communications engineering a common mathematical language for efficiency, uncertainty and reliability.
limitations: An information measure does not determine whether a message is true, meaningful or produced by intelligence.
Theoretical coding limits are not a claim that the paper supplied every practical code needed to reach them.

candidates.title: Three papers connect DNA’s double helix with experimental evidence
candidates.reason: The papers connected molecular structure with a plausible copying mechanism, linking model building and experimental evidence while leaving important biological tests and mechanisms for subsequent research.
limitations: The first Watson–Crick paper called the structure unproved pending more exact tests; it was not a complete theory of genetic function.
Only the Watson–Crick text was read in full; the accompanying papers are represented by inspected custodial and publication records.

candidates.title: Wu and the NBS team report parity violation in beta decay
candidates.reason: The experiment replaced an assumed symmetry with a measured exception, illustrating how a targeted test can change the principles used to describe nuclear processes.
limitations: The result concerns a weak-interaction decay; it does not imply that every physical process violates parity.
The report itself called for more rigorous checks and encouraged additional tests.

candidates.title: Sputnik 1 reaches Earth orbit
candidates.reason: Makes the space age a demonstrated engineering milestone and gives Soviet teams their place alongside the later American institutional and lunar achievements.
limitations: This uncrewed satellite demonstrated orbital capability, not human survival in orbit or travel beyond Earth.

candidates.title: Cocconi and Morrison propose an interstellar radio search
candidates.reason: Turns speculation about distant technological societies into a bounded observing proposal, helping explain the later radio-search tradition without implying any confirmed extraterrestrial signal.
limitations: The full unabridged Nature paper was not readable here; the January 1979 reprint explicitly omits mathematics.
Assumptions about civilizations and the historical suggestion of Martian life are not established findings.

candidates.title: Gagarin completes the first human orbital flight
candidates.reason: Shows the transition from putting machines into orbit to carrying a person, an essential capability milestone in the chronology of human exploration.
limitations: This short orbital flight did not establish the safety or feasibility of every later form of human spaceflight.
The inspected summaries establish the milestone; they are not an engineering or medical review of the entire Vostok program.

candidates.title: Katherine Johnson checks Glenn’s orbital calculations
candidates.reason: Makes a named mathematician’s contribution concrete and shows that reliable spaceflight depended on checking calculations across people, machines and a global tracking system.
limitations: The source supplies a year and preflight context, not the exact date of her calculation check.
Johnson’s verification should not be recast as sole responsibility for the mission’s navigation, software or success.

candidates.title: Bell derives a testable constraint on local hidden-variable accounts
candidates.reason: Connects a debate about quantum theory to measurable correlations, providing context for later Bell experiments while keeping physical assumptions and experimental evidence distinct.
limitations: The result constrains the specified local account; it does not rule out every hidden-variable theory.
No consciousness mechanism, spiritual connection or usable communication system follows from this theoretical paper.

candidates.title: Lonnie Zamora reports a landing near Socorro
candidates.reason: A documented landing report shows why physical traces mattered to UFO investigations, while demonstrating that unexplained observations do not establish extraordinary origins.
limitations: The reported craft and figures were not independently established by the investigators who examined the site afterward.
The Air Force reported no foreign material, abnormal radiation or identifiable propellant residue in its tests.
Unidentified is a case classification; it does not establish a particular craft, performance or origin.

candidates.title: Microwave measurements gain a hot-universe interpretation
candidates.reason: Shows how an unexplained instrumental signal became evidence about cosmic history through calibration, theoretical interpretation and explicit recognition that further measurements were still needed.
limitations: One observing frequency did not establish the full black-body spectrum.
The papers developed existing thermal-cosmology ideas; this milestone should not be described as the invention of the hot-universe hypothesis.

candidates.title: Westall school witnesses report an unusual object
candidates.reason: The Australian school report broadens the chronology beyond military encounters and illustrates how contemporary reporting, shared witnessing and later memory produce different evidence.
limitations: The inspected newspaper items are cropped reproductions, not complete issues or the original interview files.
The April 14 paper described impeded witness access; a controlled, independent interview procedure was not established in this review.
The Age proposed a balloon at the time. Later recollections and missing-record claims do not themselves identify the object.

candidates.title: Bell Burnell resolves rapidly repeating celestial radio pulses
candidates.reason: A particularly useful example of anomaly investigation: careful work by a graduate researcher and collaborators revealed a new astronomical phenomenon without establishing an artificial transmitter.
limitations: November 28 marks a resolved pulse recording, not the first trace noticed or the later publication.
Bell Burnell’s account is retrospective; this check did not reanalyze the original recordings or inspect the full Nature article.

candidates.title: Apollo 11 lands people on the Moon
candidates.reason: Establishes human surface exploration beyond Earth as an achieved capability and anchors the chronology in a mission with extensive operational records and material evidence.
limitations: The achievement depended on a large program and supporting teams, not the three astronauts alone.
The landing date should not be silently reused as the UTC date of every subsequent surface activity.

candidates.title: Vallée compares UFO encounter stories with folklore
candidates.reason: The book connects UFO research with the study of belief and narrative, making cultural interpretation an explicit part of the chronology of investigation.
limitations: Resemblance between narratives does not demonstrate a shared physical event, intelligence or mechanism.
The catalogue requires case-by-case source criticism; listing a story does not validate its historical accuracy.

candidates.title: J. Allen Hynek establishes the Center for UFO Studies
candidates.reason: Hynek gave continued civilian investigation an organizational base after Blue Book closed, separating the effort to collect and classify reports from any established explanation.
limitations: An organizational history supports chronology and stated aims; it is not an independent evaluation of research results.
Hynek’s categories describe reports and do not demonstrate the existence or origin of the reported objects.

candidates.title: Viking lands laboratories to test Martian soil
candidates.reason: Establishes an early attempt to test another world for life directly, while showing why chemical responses require competing explanations and carefully bounded conclusions.
limitations: The event date is Viking 1’s landing, not the date of every soil test or interpretation.
These local, method-dependent results neither confirmed Martian life nor demonstrated that Mars was universally lifeless.

candidates.title: Japan Air Lines flight 1628 reports unusual lights over Alaska
candidates.reason: The case shows why aviation reports must separate cockpit observations, controllers’ real-time interpretations and later instrument analysis before treating them as independent confirmation.
limitations: The initial interviews were joint crew accounts, not three independently collected confirmations of a large craft.
FAA distinguished its radar explanation from a comprehensive scientific determination of the visual report.
This review did not independently reprocess raw radar or inspect every later individual interview.

candidates.title: Belgium’s UFO reports prompt an Air Force response
candidates.reason: The Belgian wave illustrates how public reports, military sensor records and a widely reproduced photograph can acquire different evidentiary histories within one famous story.
limitations: Radar locks alone do not identify a craft or validate inferred extraordinary acceleration; original radar data were not independently reanalysed here.
The photograph and other reports have separate evidentiary histories; the admission does not explain every observation.
The Air Force summary was read in transcription, corroborated for its existence and radar locks by a UK archival guide; the signed original was not inspected.

candidates.title: Ariel School children report unusual objects and figures
candidates.reason: This Zimbabwean school case brings children’s testimony and cross-cultural interpretation into the chronology, highlighting the importance of interview timing, shared discussion and surviving records.
limitations: Hind and Callimanopulos participated in the investigations and favored an extraordinary interpretation; their publications are not independent confirmations of the reported beings.
The narratives do not establish that all accounts were collected separately before discussion; suggestibility and interviewer influence were not experimentally excluded.
Only early published reports and selected page images were inspected, not complete original drawings or unedited interview recordings.

candidates.title: Phoenix Lights — moving formations and a later flare display
candidates.reason: A landmark public controversy shows why a memorable case name can conceal different observations. Explanations need to match the particular time, location and evidence.
limitations: Neither the later flare explanation nor the aircraft account establishes the identity of every reported light. No calibrated raw imagery, complete flight logs or independent reconstruction was inspected here.
Witness recollections differ in perceived size, height and solidity. Unresolved details do not establish a non-human craft.
A 2026 internet-questionnaire paper concerns respondents’ remembered experiences and attitudes. Only its abstract was inspected; it does not supply a physical identification.

candidates.title: A draft Neanderthal genome reveals evidence of admixture
candidates.reason: Changes the account of human origins from wholly separate lineages toward documented population contact, while showing how ancient DNA can test evolutionary history.
limitations: This was a draft with limited sampling and explicit contamination controls, not a complete census of ancient or present populations.
The historical sample result must not become a timeless claim that every African population lacks Neanderthal ancestry.

candidates.title: LIGO detects a gravitational-wave signal from merging black holes
candidates.reason: Adds a way to observe the universe through spacetime strain and exemplifies the distinction between a recorded signal, model-based interpretation and a later public result.
limitations: The collaboration includes Virgo, but only the LIGO detectors observed this event.
This record reviews the published analysis; it is not an independent calibration or statistical reanalysis of strain data.

candidates.title: A Delft Bell test closes two major experimental loopholes
candidates.reason: Marks experimental progress beyond a mathematical prediction, showing how stronger controls can address loopholes without converting quantum correlations into claims about consciousness or communication.
limitations: The test still requires assumptions about independently chosen settings and the experimental/statistical model.
A Bell violation does not itself demonstrate a usable faster-than-light signalling channel or a mechanism for consciousness.

candidates.title: An adversarial collaboration tests two consciousness theories
candidates.reason: Shows consciousness research as an empirical program of explicit predictions and shared tests, offering a useful boundary between measured findings and broader philosophical interpretations.
limitations: Selected visual experiences do not cover every dimension of consciousness.
The paper acknowledges task-engagement and sampling limits and continuing interpretive disagreements.

candidates.title: William James describes the stream of thought
candidates.reason: The chapter made the organization of conscious experience an explicit object of psychological inquiry, adding a historical perspective distinct from anatomical and physical accounts.
limitations: This is a historical theoretical and introspective account, not proof of a complete mechanism of consciousness.
No inference about paranormal agency, non-human intelligence or quantum consciousness follows from the chapter.

candidates.title: Rubin and Ford map Andromeda’s rotation
candidates.reason: Makes a major astronomer’s contribution specific: new measurements and instrumentation tested how mass is distributed, helping establish a problem whose physical explanation remained open.
limitations: This was not the first suggestion of dark matter or the entire evidence base for it.
Rotation-based mass inferences did not identify a dark-matter particle.

candidates.title: Cajal reports apparently free nerve endings in the bird cerebellum
candidates.reason: The work made fine neural anatomy a source of evidence about how nervous tissue is organized, supporting a later distinction between individual cells and continuous networks.
limitations: The cautious language should be preserved; this paper did not directly image synaptic gaps or establish all mechanisms of neural communication.
A finished neuron doctrine should not be dated wholesale to this single preliminary report.

candidates.title: An engineered RNA guide directs Cas9 to cut selected DNA
candidates.reason: Marks a laboratory step from describing bacterial defence toward designing sequence-directed molecular tools, while separating mechanism, proof of concept and subsequent practical applications.
limitations: The engineered-guide demonstration was laboratory DNA cleavage, not an approved therapy or the first discovery of CRISPR.
Targeting required sequence constraints, including an adjacent PAM; the study did not establish unrestricted editing of arbitrary genomes.

candidates.title: Webb’s first science release opens its observing program
candidates.reason: Adds powerful infrared imaging and spectroscopy to the timeline’s observing tools, with international collaboration and the separation of an instrument’s readiness from particular discoveries.
limitations: These were the first science-release products, not the first photons, alignment images or every observation ever made by Webb.
A release of images or an atmospheric spectrum is not itself a detection of life.

candidates.title: Hiroshima and Nagasaki — the human cost of atomic weapons
candidates.reason: A history of expanding capability must also confront destructive uses, survivors’ experiences and responsibility. Scientific consequence is not moral endorsement.
limitations: This compact entry does not adjudicate every competing explanation of Japan’s surrender or the historical debate over alternatives.
No single precise casualty total is imposed; estimates depend on the period and consequences counted.

candidates.title: Phoenix Lights 2026 attitude-change survey
candidates.reason: Only the 2026 Phoenix questionnaire abstract was inspected. Cultural context is bounded within the Phoenix entry; a separate empirical or causal milestone is not supported by a full methods review.
limitations: Internet questionnaire, retrospective attitudes; not a physical identification.
candidates.continuation: Read the complete methods, recruitment, response limitations and subsequent assessments before interpreting attitude-change results or creating a separate event.
